newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Italy's Prodi says Bertinotti meeting went well.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says Bertinotti meeting went well.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, replying to Italian newspaper reports, said on Wednesday that a meeting in Rome with the leader of the hard left Communist Refoundation party on Tuesday had gone well.
"It went well, I won't say it went very well otherwise I would say it went too well," the centre-left prime minister told reporters accompanying him on a visit to Ukraine.
Prodi said that he had nothing more to add because "when I am abroad I speak about the domestic situation only if there are urgent issues and this is not the case."

The prime minister met Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti on Tuesday before a confidence vote in parliament to persuade him of the need for more deficit cutting to prepare Italy for the launch of a European single currency.
Bertinotti agreed to support the confidence motion in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) but repeated his concern about any further belt tightening.
Italian newspapers reported on Wednesday that the two men were still poles apart on fundamental issues.
"Prodi and Bertinotti, no understanding," declared the daily La Stampa in a front page headline.
"Bertinotti to Prodi: Neither cuts nor taxes," said the Corriere della Sera, adding that the hour-long meeting had not resolved the problems of the centre-left ruling coalition.
